title: Government doubles OMSS (D) rice sale target from 25 LMT to 50 LMT for 2026-27; 25 LMT already sold through e-auctions up to 31 October 2026
subtitle:
Stock disclosure made mandatory for all rice and paddy stocking entities across the country; stock positions to be updated every Friday
Additional allocation of Bharat Rice to NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar to expand availability, particularly in Southern States
Concurrence conveyed to five Southern States to impose stock limits on rice and paddy, wherever necessary, until 31 January 2027
body_text: The Government of India is closely monitoring food grain prices , particularly rice, and undertaking a series of policy interventions to ensure adequate domestic supplies, maintain price stability, prevent hoarding and safeguard consumer interests. In this regard, the Government has undertaken the following measures: Mandatory Disclosure of Rice and Paddy Stocks Across the Country The Government of India has issued an order dated 06.11.2026, directing all Traders/Wholesalers, Retailers, Big Chain Retailers and Processors/Millers across all States and Union Territories to declare their stock positions of rice and paddy under the following six categories: (i) Basmati Rice; (ii) Non-Basmati Premium Rice; (iii) non-Basmati Rice; (iv) Parboiled Rice; (v) Broken Rice; and (vi) Paddy. All entities stocking rice and paddy are required to disclose their stock positions every Friday on the Food Stock Portal ( https://foodstock.dfpd.gov.in ) and ensure that the information furnished is accurate and regularly updated. Any entity found unregistered on the portal or violating the prescribed stock limits shall be liable for appropriate punitive action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. Concurrence to Southern States for Imposition of Stock Limits With a view to ensuring the availability of rice to consumers at reasonable prices, particularly in the Southern States, the Government of India has conveyed its concurrence, vide communication dated 06.11.2026, to the State Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through appropriate control orders, wherever considered necessary. These stock limits shall remain in force up to 31st January 2027. The Central and State Governments will closely monitor the implementation of these measures to ensure adequate market availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing. Additional Allocation of Bharat Rice to Expand Market Availability The Government of India is allocating additional quantities of ‘Bharat Rice’ to three agencies, NAFED, NCCF and Kendriya Bhandar with the objective of substantially expanding its sale and availability across the country, particularly in the Southern States. The agencies have also been directed to explore all possible distribution channels to ensure wider reach and easy accessibility of ‘Bharat Rice’ to consumers. The initiative is expected to augment market supplies, improve consumer access to rice at affordable prices and contribute to moderating retail prices. Doubling of Rice Sale Target Under OMSS (D) for 2026-27 The Government of India has doubled the target quantity of rice for sale through e-auction under the Open Market Sale Scheme (Domestic) [OMSS (D)] for 2026-27, increasing it from 25 LMT to 50 Maturing FY 2026-27 (up to 31.10.2026), a total of 25 LMT of rice has been sold to private parties through OMSS (D) e-auctions, as against 11 LMT during the corresponding period of the previous financial year. This reflects a significant increase in market supplies through the intervention. These measures reaffirm the Government's commitment to ensuring adequate availability of essential food commodities, maintaining price stability and safeguarding consumer interests across the country. *** RT/IA/RP
